topStories.headline: Neighbors Pack Church to Push Back on Eight-Story Safeway Tower at Ocean Beach
topStories.dek: A proposed 562-unit housing development above the Outer Richmond's La Playa Safeway has ignited a community firestorm, with residents arguing state streamlining laws have stripped them of any real say.
topStories.body:
<cite index="71-4">Due to state law, the proposed housing development to replace the Safeway on La Playa Street with a new store and 562 units of housing has been "streamlined," restricting the input to city officials from the residents of that neighborhood.</cite> That legal reality did not stop neighbors from showing up.

<cite index="71-5">The Planning Association for the Richmond (PAR) gave local residents the opportunity to voice either their opposition or support for the proposal by hosting a meeting at St. John's Presbyterian Church on Lake Street at the end of September.</cite> <cite index="68-3,68-4">About 60 people heard speakers discuss the proposed eight-story Safeway redevelopment project at 850 La Playa St. near Ocean Beach. The takeaway from those speakers: the project will be too large, too tall, and out of scale for the neighborhood.</cite>

<cite index="69-5,69-6">Align Real Estate is the project sponsor, working on behalf of the property owner, Albertsons Companies. The roughly 85-foot-tall structure is expected to yield around 820,000 square feet, including 520,600 square feet for housing, 79,750 square feet of retail, and 179,900 square feet for parking.</cite> <cite index="74-9,74-10">The proposal calls for 562 residential units, up from previous plans for 526. Of those 562 units, 113 will be deed-restricted as affordable housing for residents earning between 50 percent and 80 percent of the area's median income.</cite>

<cite index="68-14,68-15">There is little Richmond residents can do to shape the project. Align Real Estate, which has partnered with Safeway's parent company to develop the site and many other Safeways across the city, is taking advantage of state streamlining laws</cite> — including Senate Bill 330 and the State Density Bonus Law — that limit local discretionary review. <cite index="69-13">The application invokes Senate Bill 330 and the State Density Bonus Law to increase residential capacity and streamline the approval process.</cite>

The debate reflects a tension playing out across San Francisco's western neighborhoods, where longtime residents see a wave of larger, denser development arriving on corridors they have long considered stable. The La Playa project has no scheduled Planning Commission hearing date as of this week, and the investigation into community input options continues.

topStories.headline: 80-Year-Old Man Killed by Tow Truck at Anza and Arguello — a Stretch City Officials Long Flagged as Dangerous
topStories.dek: Yuan Jun Zhu died September 28 at a crosswalk near Rossi Playground, reigniting demands for protected infrastructure on one of the Richmond's most hazardous corridors.
topStories.body:
<cite index="99-5,99-6,99-7">The city medical examiner identified the victim as 80-year-old Yuan Jun Zhu. The vehicle was a tow truck, the advocacy group Walk San Francisco said, citing SFPD. The collision occurred at the intersection of Anza Street and Arguello Boulevard, near Rossi Pool and Playground.</cite>

<cite index="40-3,40-4,40-5,40-6">On September 28, 2026, at approximately 2:08 p.m., San Francisco Police officers from Richmond Station responded to the intersection of Anza Street and Arguello Boulevard regarding a vehicle collision involving a pedestrian. Officers arrived on scene and rendered aid. Paramedics transported the pedestrian to a nearby hospital with life-threatening injuries. Despite lifesaving efforts, the pedestrian succumbed to their injuries and was declared deceased at the hospital.</cite> <cite index="44-12">The incident marks San Francisco's 13th pedestrian death of 2026, according to Walk SF.</cite>

<cite index="98-10,98-11">The crash happened beside Angelo J. Rossi Playground, which includes a children's play area, pool, and sports facilities. Roosevelt Middle School is also located on Arguello Boulevard.</cite> <cite index="98-13,98-14">The agency said the portion of Arguello north of Geary Boulevard remains on the city's current High Injury Network, a collection of streets where fatal and severe transportation collisions occur most frequently. The agency currently lists the project status as "Planning."</cite>

<cite index="99-11">Walk SF's spokesperson said police told her that the truck driver struck the pedestrian in a crosswalk as the driver turned from Arguello Boulevard onto Anza Street.</cite> <cite index="40-7,40-8,40-9,40-10">The driver of the vehicle involved remained on scene and is cooperating with the investigation. SFPD's Traffic Collision Investigations Unit is currently investigating the incident. At this time, no arrests have been made. This remains an open and active investigation.</cite>

In a Streetsblog San Francisco op-ed published October 6, advocates called on Mayor Lurie to act immediately, arguing that turns on red should be prohibited at Anza and Arguello and that the corridor's unprotected bike lanes should be upgraded. <cite index="102-9,102-10">While the crosswalks at the intersection of Arguello and Anza are marked, turns on red are allowed — as they are at every traffic light on Arguello and Anza. Both streets are 56 feet wide, an unnecessarily long crossing distance that makes crashes more likely.</cite>

topStories.headline: Jack Dorsey's Sea Cliff Renovation Drags Into Its 14th Year — and His Billionaire Neighbors Are Over It
topStories.dek: The Block CEO's two adjoining El Camino del Mar properties have been under almost continuous construction since 2012, turning one of San Francisco's quietest streets into a round-the-clock work site.
topStories.body:
<cite index="115-4,115-5">Jack Dorsey bought his first Sea Cliff property in February 2012 for $9.99 million, and in the time since, the San Francisco home has barely gone a stretch without scaffolding, a permit filing, or a crew on site. Nearly 14 years later, work is still happening in some form on the two adjoining lots the tech entrepreneur now owns on El Camino del Mar, a stretch of street perched above the Pacific Ocean with sweeping views of the Golden Gate Bridge.</cite>

<cite index="115-8">In November 2018, Dorsey added the neighboring parcel at 840 El Camino del Mar for $21.9 million, bringing his combined investment in the two lots to roughly $31.9 million across approximately 1.21 acres.</cite> <cite index="121-10,121-11,121-12">Architectural plans reveal an elaborate coastal sanctuary featuring three vegetation-covered roofs, reclaimed redwood siding, stonework, and expansive windows overlooking the ocean. The primary bedroom opens onto a private hot tub perched above the Pacific, while other amenities include a steam room, a plunge pool, and an extensive sauna complex. There is also a gym with a punching bag, an outdoor fire pit, cedar benches, and 34 solar panels.</cite>

<cite index="117-9,117-10,117-11">On a recent visit, booming construction work and diesel fumes pierced through the sea breeze. Despite being one of America's most desirable neighborhoods, Sea Cliff currently resembles a building site with a view. Just down the road from Dorsey's two homes on El Camino del Mar, a mansion was completely shrouded in black netting.</cite> <cite index="118-11">Along the eight-block stretch of El Camino del Mar, at least 24 homes have filed building permits since the beginning of 2025, according to planning documents.</cite>

The Dorsey project has drawn renewed attention from neighbors who describe years of noise and disruption with no clear end date. <cite index="118-10">The prestigious neighborhood has counted late comedian Robin Williams and actress Sharon Stone among its residents, and is also home to Salesforce co-founder Marc Benioff and billionaire investor Tom Steyer.</cite> Dorsey, who now runs financial technology company Block, has not publicly commented on the construction timeline.

events.title: Clement Street Art Fair & Broke-Ass Stuart Day
events.location: Clement Street between 6th and 8th Avenues, Inner Richmond
events.description: <cite index="25-2,25-3">The Inner Richmond neighborhood will come alive for the 3rd annual Clement Street Art Fair. Clement Street — from 6th to 8th Avenues — will close to traffic to provide a fun-filled day of art activations, live music, local makers, and community building.</cite> <cite index="25-5">The fair will offer activities including a bike fix-it station, make-and-take crafts from Workshop SF, live printing by Fleetwood, and a community art project.</cite>

events.title: Free Yoga in the Park (presented by Sutter Health)
events.description: <cite index="126-7,126-8,126-9">One of the first initiatives of the new Sutter Health–Presidio Trust partnership, this free weekly wellness series runs from Sept. 13 through Nov. 22 at Outpost Meadow in collaboration with Sports Basement. Open to participants of all ages and abilities, the classes offer opportunities for movement, mindfulness, and community. Each session can accommodate up to 50 participants, with advance registration required.</cite>

events.title: Fort Point History Talk
events.location: Fort Point, under the Golden Gate Bridge, Presidio
events.description: <cite index="1-3">A Golden Gate National Recreation Area Park Ranger leads a brief history discussion at Fort Point, the only brick Civil War-era fort on the West Coast, situated beneath the Golden Gate Bridge.</cite> Free and open to all park visitors.

events.title: District 1 Richmond Family Summit
events.location: Richmond Recreation Center, 251 18th Ave, San Francisco
events.description: <cite index="38-6,38-7">The District 1 Richmond Family Summit is part of the "This Is Your City: Family Summit Series," which invites families, caregivers, young people, and community members from across San Francisco to help shape the future of the city.</cite> <cite index="16-2">District 1 neighborhoods include Inner Richmond, Central Richmond, Outer Richmond, Vista del Mar, and Seacliff.</cite> Free to attend.

events.title: 250 Years on the Presidio — Guided History Walk
events.location: Presidio Visitor Center, 210 Lincoln Blvd, Presidio
events.description: <cite index="109-4,109-5">Join National Park Service Rangers for a guided walk through Presidio Tunnel Tops and the historic Main Post, starting at the Presidio Visitor Center. This half-mile walk explores the layered history of the park, from the time of the Ohlone people through Spanish and U.S. Army occupation to its present role as a national park site.</cite> Free; part of the Presidio's yearlong 250th anniversary programming.

events.title: Park Ranger Campfire Talks at Presidio Tunnel Tops
events.location: Campfire Circle, Presidio Tunnel Tops, Presidio
events.description: <cite index="32-4">National Park Service rangers lead free talks at Presidio Tunnel Tops' Campfire Circle, covering the park's history, ecology, and stories.</cite> Free and drop-in; no registration required.

moreNews.headline: Inner Richmond Car Wash Site Proposed for 38-Unit, Eight-Story Building
moreNews.body: <cite index="87-4">A shuttered car wash at the corner of Collins Street and Geary Boulevard in San Francisco's Inner Richmond could soon give way to an eight-story building with 38 apartments, according to newly revealed plans for the site revealed on October 9, 2026.</cite> <cite index="87-6,87-7">The current design includes an articulated facade with light tan and blue panels wrapped around floor-to-ceiling windows. The property sits near the USF Lone Mountain campus and the City Center shopping mall, placing it in a dense pocket of the Inner Richmond.</cite> The project relies on California's State Density Bonus Law to increase height and unit count above what base zoning would allow.

moreNews.headline: Presidio Trust Lands First-Ever Corporate Sponsor in Sutter Health Partnership
moreNews.body: <cite index="125-1">As the Presidio Trust's Founding Partner and Official Healthcare Partner, Sutter Health became the first nonprofit healthcare organization to hold an official partnership designation with a U.S. national park site, announced September 16, 2026.</cite> <cite index="127-14,127-15">The financial commitment from Sutter Health is different from a straight donation in that it will guarantee Sutter defined marketing rights and benefits. The deal will extend to trail management and forestry conservation, native habitat restoration, investment in sustainable transportation infrastructure, and support for community events and programs.</cite> The partnership's inaugural program — free weekly yoga at Outpost Meadow — runs Sundays through November 22.

restaurants.name: Burma Superstar
restaurants.description: The original 1992 Inner Richmond location that popularized Burmese cuisine in San Francisco, famous for its tea leaf salad and perpetual lines.

restaurants.name: Mandalay Restaurant
restaurants.description: San Francisco's oldest running Burmese restaurant, open since 1984 and named a James Beard America's Classic in 2024.

restaurants.name: Dalida
restaurants.description: Upscale Eastern Mediterranean dining in the Presidio's Main Post, with a porch overlooking the parade lawn stretching toward Alcatraz.

restaurants.name: Kitchen Istanbul
restaurants.description: A beloved Inner Richmond Turkish restaurant celebrated by sommeliers for its impeccable natural wine list and Eastern Mediterranean cooking.

restaurants.name: Lokma
restaurants.description: Cozy Outer Richmond spot serving a modern California-Turkish menu of shared plates in a brick-walled dining room with excellent brunch on weekends.

restaurants.name: Aziza
restaurants.description: Acclaimed Moroccan restaurant on Geary Boulevard serving inventive contemporary Moroccan cuisine in an elegant, warmly lit setting.

restaurants.name: Bella Trattoria
restaurants.description: Long-running Inner Richmond Italian restaurant specializing in cucina napolitana, with housemade pastas and a loyal neighborhood following since 1996.

restaurants.name: Fiorella
restaurants.description: Neighborhood Italian wine bar and pizzeria known for blistered wood-fired pies and a lively Outer Richmond dining room.

restaurants.name: Rose Pizzeria
restaurants.description: Berkeley's nationally acclaimed pizzeria opened its first San Francisco outpost at the east end of Clement Street in April 2026, serving Neapolitan and Roman-style pies daily.

restaurants.name: Pizzetta 211
restaurants.description: Small, much-loved Outer Richmond pizzeria serving a short rotating menu of thin-crust seasonal pies in an intimate space with outdoor parklet seating.

restaurants.name: B Star
restaurants.description: Burma Superstar's sister restaurant offering a more eclectic, fusion-forward Burmese menu in a slightly more relaxed setting on Clement Street.

restaurants.name: Mamahuhu
restaurants.description: Bright and popular Clement Street spot serving approachable, flavor-forward Chinese-American dishes including mapo tofu and mala cucumbers.

restaurants.name: Hokkaido Sashimi Marketplace
restaurants.description: Inner Richmond counter serving fresh sashimi and to-go sushi rolls, a popular stop before a picnic in Golden Gate Park.

restaurants.name: Hard Knox Cafe
restaurants.description: Casual Outer Richmond diner serving Southern staples—fried chicken, cornbread muffins, and daily brunch until 3 p.m.—at honest prices.

restaurants.name: Kissaten Hi-Fi
restaurants.description: New Inner Richmond café rooted in the Japanese kissaten tradition, serving single-cultivar matcha and Filipino-inspired coffee in a slow, intentional setting.

hotels.name: Inn at the Presidio
hotels.description: The first hotel to open inside the Presidio national park site, housed in a beautifully restored 1903 Georgian Revival building with bay-view suites, complimentary breakfast, and evening wine receptions.

hotels.name: Lodge at the Presidio
hotels.description: Historic barracks building converted into a contemporary 42-room hotel on the Presidio's Main Post, offering free breakfast, forest and bay views, and a shuttle downtown.

hotels.name: Geary Parkway Motel
hotels.description: Renovated 20-room motel on Geary Boulevard offering free to-go breakfast and on-site parking within walking distance of Golden Gate Park.

shops.name: Green Apple Books
shops.description: Iconic Richmond District bookstore founded in 1967, stocking new and used titles across 8,000 square feet at the corner of Clement and Sixth Avenue.

shops.name: Park Life
shops.description: Inner Richmond design store and rotating gallery selling art books, locally made goods, prints, apparel, and limited-edition artist collaborations.

shops.name: Foggy Notion
shops.description: Inviting Clement Street boutique selling handcrafted ceramics, stationery, and locally made gifts with a warm, artisan-focused curation.

shops.name: Gaslight & Shadows Antiques
shops.description: Outer Richmond antique shop on Clement Street with a passionately curated selection of vintage objects and collectibles.

shops.name: Nijiya Market
shops.description: Well-stocked Japanese supermarket carrying fresh sushi-grade fish, Japanese pantry staples, and prepared foods popular with the neighborhood's Japanese community.

shops.name: New May Wah Supermarket
shops.description: Large Asian grocery destination on Clement Street with an extensive range of Chinese, Southeast Asian, and other imported pantry items.

shops.name: Jane Consignment
shops.description: Outer Richmond consignment shop on Clement Street carrying quality pre-owned women's clothing and accessories.

shops.name: Love Street Vintage
shops.description: Curated vintage clothing boutique on Clement Street carrying a wide selection of women's vintage apparel and accessories.

artEntertainment.name: Walt Disney Family Museum
artEntertainment.description: Forty-thousand-square-foot museum in the Presidio dedicated to the life and legacy of Walt Disney, with ten interactive galleries, Disney film screenings, and a new exhibition opening October 23 tracing artist Eyvind Earle's career.

artEntertainment.name: Legion of Honor
artEntertainment.description: Beaux-Arts museum in Lincoln Park founded in 1924, housing 6,000 years of European art, over 70 Rodin sculptures, and one of the largest prints-and-drawings collections in the country.

artEntertainment.name: Park Life Gallery
artEntertainment.type: Contemporary art gallery and design store
artEntertainment.description: Inner Richmond gallery space behind the Park Life store mounting rotating exhibitions of local and national artists, with about ten shows per year.

artEntertainment.name: Avenue 12 Gallery
artEntertainment.description: Small Inner Richmond gallery active in the Bay Area arts community, exhibiting local artists and Bay Area subject matter.

artEntertainment.name: Andy Goldsworthy Sculpture Trail
artEntertainment.description: Four permanent works by British sculptor Andy Goldsworthy installed across the Presidio—Wood Line, Spire, Earth Wall, and Tree Fall—all freely accessible on foot.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Officers' Club
artEntertainment.description: One of the oldest buildings in San Francisco, the adobe-walled Officers' Club on the Presidio's Main Post houses free museum galleries exploring the site's 250-year history.

gymsRecreation.name: Richmond District YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: Full-service YMCA branch in the Inner Richmond offering cardio equipment, weight rooms, yoga classes, and youth programs for the neighborhood.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Community YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: YMCA branch inside the Presidio offering fitness classes, youth programs, and access to the Letterman Aquatics Center pool.

gymsRecreation.name: Folk Yoga Richmond
gymsRecreation.description: Intimate yoga studio at 182 Sixth Avenue offering vinyasa flow, power flow, prenatal yoga, and $15 community classes as part of San Francisco's largest locally owned yoga network.

gymsRecreation.name: Hot Yoga Plus
gymsRecreation.description: Outer Richmond studio on Geary Boulevard specializing in Bikram 26&2 yoga and Inferno Hot Pilates in a heated environment.

gymsRecreation.name: The Yoga Shala SF – Balboa Street
gymsRecreation.description: Richmond-area heated vinyasa yoga studio on Balboa Street, created for practitioners to thrive through consistent, community-oriented practice.

gymsRecreation.name: F45 Training
gymsRecreation.description: Franchise functional fitness studio on Geary Boulevard offering fast-paced group circuit workouts with attentive form coaching.

gymsRecreation.name: Live Fit Gym – Inner Richmond
gymsRecreation.description: Community gym at Arguello Boulevard offering strength training, power flow yoga, and fitness classes led by instructors including a licensed doctor of physical therapy.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Golf Course
gymsRecreation.description: Consistently ranked among the nation's top public courses, this 18-hole championship layout winds through eucalyptus and Monterey pine in the Presidio national park.

gymsRecreation.name: Golden Gate Park
gymsRecreation.description: More than 1,000 acres of meadows, trails, sports courts, and cultural institutions bordering the Richmond neighborhoods, used daily for running, cycling, tennis, and lawn sports.
